species.stagePolicy: Do not pretend there is one universal Yellowfin proportion. Size class and geographic morphometric variation remain explicit variables.

coordinateContract.normalization: inferred fork length when the caudal-upper/lower shared trailing notch is valid; otherwise report total longitudinal extent and block candidate acceptance

topologyInterpretation.rule: Raw connected-component order is not anatomical identity. Thin fins stored as disconnected positive-X and negative-X sheets must be paired by mirrored centroid, identical topology, longitudinal range, attachment root and height before naming the first or second dorsal fin.
topologyInterpretation.acceptance: The first and second dorsal fins must each resolve to two symmetric sheets. Deforming only one sheet is a hard failure even when a one-sided metric reaches its target.

populationVariation.source: William F. Royce, A morphometric study of yellowfin Thunnus albacares, 4,180 specimens
populationVariation.rule: Use envelopes and a declared adult phenotype; never label one exact ratio as species truth.

evidencePolicy.provisionalRule: Engineering envelopes are candidate controls, not published species limits. They must remain labeled provisional until visual and morphometric acceptance.

correctionOrder: audit frozen rest geometry, regions, bind skeleton and animation channels
resolve mirrored fin sheets into anatomical surface pairs before reading fin identity or metrics
lock fork-length inference and baseline morphometrics
correct body depth distribution and head transition
correct caudal peduncle and keel support without weakening the tail root
correct pectoral, second dorsal and anal fin proportions for the declared adult phenotype
preserve finlet count unless evidence proves a segmentation error
propagate the same smooth rest-space deformation to vertices, bind joints and translation animation data
run rest-pose, Swim, material, silhouette and console-zero browser QA
